solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Developed area died in the last month

parts.note: A is the standard abbreviation for area
d. is the abbreviation for died, as in family trees
ult., short for ultimo, is old business-letter Latin for 'of last month'

explanation.surface: A district that was built up and then went into decline over the past few weeks.
explanation.walkthrough: ULT is the abbreviation for ultimo, once used in letters to mean 'of last month' (as in 'your letter of the 3rd ult.').
explanation.definitionFit: A grown-up creature has fully matured, so 'developed' serves as an adjective meaning fully grown.

clue.text: Signature dish's culmination — ragout mixed with a touch of parsley

indicators.note: something mixed has been stirred together, so the letters lose their original order

parts.note: taken as written, as anagram material
taken as written; also part of the mix

indicators.note: a mere touch is the smallest taste, so only the opening letter is taken

parts.note: the opening letter of the herb

indicators.note: a culmination is the final point, so only the closing letter is wanted

parts.note: the final letter of 'dish'

explanation.surface: A chef's signature dish is finished off with a stew and a sprinkle of parsley.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Signature dish' reads as one culinary phrase, but the definition stops after 'Signature'. The 'a' in 'with a touch' joins the anagram along with P, and H is tacked on at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: A celebrity's handwritten name given to a fan is a signature, so the two words are synonyms.

clue.text: Somewhat wasted, falling short before week 8

indicators.note: coming before means standing in front, so the pieces run in the order given

parts.note: to fall short of a target is to come in under it
W is the abbreviation for week
the number written as a word

explanation.surface: Someone a little drunk and not quite making it through to the eighth week of a course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wasted' suggests drunkenness, but here it means thin and emaciated; 'somewhat' softens it to a mild degree.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who is too light for their height looks thin, a milder form of being emaciated or wasted away.

clue.text: Amused tense childish little daughter

parts.note: T is the grammar abbreviation for tense
ickle is British baby talk for little
D is the abbreviation for daughter

explanation.surface: A parent nervously entertained by their small daughter's antics.
explanation.walkthrough: ICKLE is a cutesy British way of saying 'little', the sort of word used to toddlers, hence 'childish'.
explanation.definitionFit: To be tickled, in the informal sense, is to be pleased or entertained, as in 'tickled pink'.

clue.text: About to cut in due to false instruction

indicators.note: to cut in is to push into the middle of something, so one piece goes inside another
something false is not the real arrangement, so these letters must be reordered

parts.note: taken as written, as anagram material
ca. is short for circa, Latin for about

explanation.surface: Someone interrupting because a set of directions turned out to be wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' looks like part of the instruction to cut in, but it is part of the anagram material, with 'cut' alone doing the inserting work alongside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Schooling and teaching are what instruction provides, so the noun education is a near synonym.

clue.text: Antelope from Afghanistan, for one

parts.note: Afghanistan lies to the east of Britain, so it stands for E, eastern
Afghanistan is one example of a country or land

explanation.surface: An antelope that comes from Afghanistan.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'Afghanistan, for one' as 'an E land': E is east, and Afghanistan lies east of Britain. The surface wrongly implies the animal lives there; it is African.
explanation.definitionFit: The eland is a large African antelope with spiral horns, so the clue gives a species for its family.

clue.text: Freed of nuts and gluten

indicators.note: nuts means crazy, and crazy letters are jumbled out of their proper places

parts.note: taken as written, as anagram material

explanation.surface: A product label promising it is free of nuts and gluten, as for allergy sufferers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nuts and gluten' reads as a list of allergens, but 'nuts' is the signal to rearrange the letters of 'and gluten'.
explanation.definitionFit: Knotted string or hair, once loosened, has been released from its tangles, so freed suits it.

clue.text: Secret weapon hidden in jail uniform? On the contrary

indicators.note: something hidden in a place sits inside it, so one piece will enclose another
this flips the stated relationship, so the enclosing piece and the enclosed piece swap roles

parts.note: an arm is a weapon, as in firearm
the can is slang for prison
Uniform is U in the NATO alphabet

explanation.surface: A smuggled weapon concealed in a prisoner's clothes.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface hides the weapon inside the prison clothing; 'On the contrary' swaps the roles, so the jail and the uniform go inside the weapon.
explanation.definitionFit: An arcanum is a mystery known only to initiates, so as a noun it is a synonym for a secret.

clue.text: Fish going under keels, essentially

indicators.note: the essence of something is its core, so only the central letter of each word counts

parts.note: the central letter of a five-letter word
the central letter of a five-letter word
the central letter of a five-letter word

explanation.surface: A fish swimming beneath the keels of boats.
explanation.walkthrough: Each of the three words after the definition has five letters, so each has a single central letter to contribute.
explanation.definitionFit: The ide, also called the orfe, is a European freshwater species of the carp family, a crossword regular.

clue.text: Point of dissertation or thesis only partly considered

indicators.note: if only part of a phrase is looked at, the answer is a stretch within it

parts.note: spans the end of the first word, the whole of the second and the start of the third

explanation.surface: A student complaining that the main argument of their dissertation was only half read.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Point of dissertation' looks like the definition, meaning its argument; only 'Point' defines, in its compass sense. The letters run dissertatio(N OR TH)esis.
explanation.definitionFit: The four cardinal points of the compass are north, south, east and west, so this is one example.

clue.text: Chad imports European spread

indicators.note: to import is to bring something inside, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: TD is the international vehicle code for Chad
E is the abbreviation for European

explanation.surface: An African country bringing in a foodstuff such as margarine from Europe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spread' looks like a noun for butter or jam, but here it is a verb: to ted is to spread out mown grass to dry as hay.
explanation.definitionFit: Farmers ted hay by tossing and scattering it across the field, a dialect or farming sense of spreading out.

clue.text: Reel in and catch fighting cock

indicators.note: things fighting are thrown about in a scuffle, so the letters end up in a new order

parts.note: taken as written, as anagram material
taken as written, as anagram material

explanation.surface: An angler told to land a fish, or else a scene of capturing a fighting cockerel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fighting cock' reads as a single phrase, but 'fighting' is the signal to rearrange the earlier words, leaving 'cock' as the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Chanticleer is the traditional name of the rooster in fables such as Chaucer's Nun's Priest's Tale, a literary name for a male fowl.

clue.text: Jumbled clothing went first

parts.note: garb is clothing, a costume or dress
to lead is to go at the front

explanation.surface: A messy pile of clothes, and someone going ahead of the others.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jumbled' looks like it might signal a rearrangement of 'clothing', but it is the definition, and the wordplay is a plain two-part build.
explanation.definitionFit: A garbled message is mixed up and confused, so the two adjectives are close synonyms.

clue.text: Back in hotel, just having gone round ancient city

indicators.note: going back means running the opposite way, so the next word is read right to left

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: turning right round leaves something facing the other way, so its letters run backwards

parts.note: just and even both mean fair
Hotel is H in the NATO alphabet

explanation.surface: A traveller returning to their hotel after a quick tour of an old city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Back in hotel' reads as returning to a hotel, but 'Back' turns 'in' around, and H is placed at the end after the turned-round EVEN.
explanation.definitionFit: Nineveh was the capital of ancient Assyria, on the Tigris, so it is an example of an old city.

clue.text: Nothing in Salvador Dali's latest old rubbish evokes arduous experience

indicators.note: rubbish is junk thrown together, so the letters are scrambled into a new order

parts.note: nothing is zero, shaped like O
taken as written, as anagram material

indicators.note: the latest thing is the most recent, at the very end, so only the final letter is used

parts.note: the final letter of the painter's surname
O is the abbreviation for old

explanation.surface: A critic dismissing a Dalí painting as worthless old rubbish that recalls an ordeal.
explanation.walkthrough: Salvador Dalí seems to be the subject, but his first name is just anagram material; the O for nothing sits inside it before everything is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: The Via Dolorosa is the route Christ walked to the crucifixion, so figuratively it means any painful ordeal or trial.

clue.text: Obsessed Executive Committee 25 stops, according to private narrative

indicators.note: a stopper plugs a gap from inside, so these pieces fill the middle of another

parts.note: anal, in the informal sense, means fussily obsessive
the initial letters of the two words
the answer to 25 down in this puzzle

explanation.surface: A fixated committee halting proceedings on the basis of someone's personal story.
explanation.walkthrough: The '25' is a cross-reference: write in the answer to 25 down, which is DOT, and use it with EC as the plug.
explanation.definitionFit: Anecdotal evidence rests on personal stories and hearsay rather than research, so it is based on private accounts.

clue.text: Unspecified number in Italy following opera conductor

indicators.note: what follows comes later in the line, so the earlier pieces are placed after the later-named one

parts.note: Tosca is Puccini's opera
n stands for an unspecified number in maths
taken as written
I is the international vehicle code for Italy

explanation.surface: Some number of Italians attend an opera conducted by a maestro.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' looks like a placement instruction, but it is simply taken as written between N and I.
explanation.definitionFit: Arturo Toscanini was a celebrated Italian maestro, so this is an example of someone who leads an orchestra.

clue.text: Substantial worry occupies host in the second half?

indicators.note: to occupy a place is to sit inside it, so one piece goes within the other
only the latter half of the word is kept, its closing letters

parts.note: a host is an army; its second half is kept
'what's eating you?' means 'what's worrying you?'

explanation.surface: A host fretting during the second half of a party or a match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Host' here means a large army, as in 'a heavenly host', not someone giving a party. Its last two letters wrap around EAT.
explanation.definitionFit: A meaty issue or role has plenty of substance to it, so the adjectives are synonyms in that figurative sense.

clue.text: Historic county long ago hosting king and his new queen

indicators.note: a host takes guests inside, so one piece holds the others within it

parts.note: 'days of yore' are times long past

indicators.note: something new is a fresh version, so the letters take a different arrangement

parts.note: K is king in chess notation
taken as written, as anagram material
R for regina, Latin for queen

explanation.surface: An old English county once welcoming a monarch and his new bride.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Historic county' is the definition; Yorkshire, in northern England, was split up in 1974, so it is a historic county. The rest goes inside YORE between its R and E.
explanation.definitionFit: Yorkshire is England's largest traditional shire, now divided for administration, so it is an example of an old county.

clue.text: Anticyclones mainly struck trains in Long Beach suburbs

indicators.note: mainly means for the most part, so the word loses its last letter

parts.note: struck means hit; drop the final letter

indicators.note: a train is the trailing tail of a gown, so only the tail letter of each word is taken

parts.note: the final letter of the word
the final letter of the word
the final letter of the word

explanation.surface: Storms batter railway services in the outskirts of the Californian city of Long Beach.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trains' is a noun in the surface but works as a word for tails: the end letters of Long, Beach and suburbs.
explanation.definitionFit: Meteorologists call areas of high pressure highs, and an anticyclone is exactly such a pressure system.

clue.text: Wherein winkles could be found using spades, also rod

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for spades in card games
and and also both add something more
a bar is a rod of metal

explanation.surface: Directions for digging up winkles on the shore with spades and a pole.
explanation.walkthrough: Spades and a rod sound like the tools for digging out shellfish, but they are just letter sources. Winkles are small edible sea snails.
explanation.definitionFit: A ridge of sand in shallow coastal water is a habitat where shellfish such as periwinkles may live.

clue.text: Battle crest buried in southern heath

indicators.note: something buried lies inside the ground, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for southern
a moor is open heathland
the crest of a ridge is its top edge

explanation.surface: A family coat of arms found buried in heathland in the south, perhaps after a battle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Battle crest' reads as a heraldic emblem; the definition stops at 'Battle', and 'crest' is the top of a ridge. Sedgemoor is in Somerset, in south-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: The Battle of Sedgemoor in Somerset in 1685 ended the Monmouth Rebellion, so it is an example of a military engagement.

clue.text: Is in France, Oregon, Israel and Portuguese resort

parts.note: est is French for 'is'
OR is the US postal code for Oregon
IL is the country code for Israel

explanation.surface: A list of places where something is found: France, Oregon, Israel and a seaside town in Portugal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Is in France' is not a location but a translation: the French word for 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Estoril is a seaside town near Lisbon known for its casino and beaches, an example of a holiday spot in Portugal.

clue.text: Receiver's data transmission ultimately not available after 10

indicators.note: coming after means following behind, so this piece is placed later
ultimately means in the end, so only the closing letter of each word is kept

parts.note: the final letter of the word
the final letter of the word
the number written as a word
n/a is the standard abbreviation for not available

explanation.surface: A radio receiver's data feed eventually cutting out after ten o'clock.
explanation.walkthrough: '10' looks like a cross-reference to 10 across, but it is the plain number. The 's after 'Receiver' stands for 'is', joining definition to wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: An aerial picks up radio signals, so it is the part of a set that does the receiving.

clue.text: American left worthless picture book

parts.note: A is the abbreviation for American
L is the abbreviation for left
bum as an adjective means of poor quality, as in a bum deal

explanation.surface: An American abandoning a poor-quality illustrated book.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Left' looks like a verb (abandoned), but it is just the abbreviation L.
explanation.definitionFit: A photo album is a bound volume for holding photographs, so it is a book of pictures.

clue.text: Sanctimonious about note being lamentable

indicators.note: about means around, so one piece wraps round another

parts.note: pious can mean self-righteous or holier-than-thou
te is a note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: A holier-than-thou person writing a pitiful note.
explanation.walkthrough: 'note' looks like a written message, but it is one of the do-re-mi syllables, written te in British usage (ti in American).
explanation.definitionFit: Something piteous arouses pity, which is what a lamentable or pitiful state of affairs also does.

clue.text: Chubby group of pilots perhaps extremely greedy

parts.note: pilot whales swim in groups called pods; 'perhaps' marks pilots as an example of whale

indicators.note: the extremes of something are its two ends, so only the outer letters are kept

parts.note: the first and last letters of the word

explanation.surface: A tubby squadron of aviators who are very gluttonous.
explanation.walkthrough: The pilots are not aviators but pilot whales, which travel in pods.
explanation.definitionFit: A podgy person is short and plump, so the two informal adjectives are synonyms.

clue.text: Daftly, 50% of risk doubled by nutritious food

indicators.note: done daftly means done foolishly and out of order, so the letters are rearranged
half of a four-letter word is its opening pair of letters

parts.note: the opening half of the word
taken as written, as anagram material

explanation.surface: A foolish warning that risk is twice as high when you eat healthy food.
explanation.walkthrough: 'doubled by' reads as part of the sentence, but both words are anagram material along with RI.
explanation.definitionFit: Protein-rich food that helps the body grow strong was once advertised as a body-builder, a dated food-marketing term.

clue.text: Mark's party time

parts.note: a do is a party or celebration
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: It is time for Mark's party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mark' looks like a man's name, but it is the definition; the 's stands for 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: A small round spot made with a pen is a kind of mark, so the nouns are synonyms.

clue.text: Boxing association withdraws belt

indicators.note: to withdraw is to pull back, so the letters run the other way

parts.note: the IBO is the International Boxing Organization

explanation.surface: A boxing body strips a champion of their title belt.
explanation.walkthrough: In boxing a belt is a championship title, but here it is the Japanese garment.
explanation.definitionFit: An obi is the broad sash tied around a kimono, so it is a kind of waistband.

clue.text: In one month, bird has sex after motherhood

indicators.note: to be in something is to sit inside it, so one piece holds the others

parts.note: May is one of the twelve months

indicators.note: coming after means following behind, so this piece is placed later

parts.note: a tern is a seabird
it is slang for sex or sex appeal

explanation.surface: In springtime, a bird mates after hatching young.
explanation.walkthrough: IT for sex is a crossword staple, from old slang for sex appeal; TERN then IT go inside MAY.
explanation.definitionFit: Maternity is the state of being a mother, so the two nouns are synonyms.

clue.text: Bequeath 17th-century bible found in shelter

indicators.note: something found in a place lies inside it, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: the lee is the sheltered side, away from the wind
the AV, or Authorized Version, is the King James Bible of 1611

explanation.surface: Someone leaving a valuable old bible, discovered in a hut, in their will.
explanation.walkthrough: AV stands for the Authorized Version of 1611, better known as the King James Bible.
explanation.definitionFit: To bequeath something is to hand it on to heirs in a will, which is what leaving it to them means.
